purpose: Presents compact labels, filters, choices, removable collections, standalone buttons and links, or selected tags with sub-label menus.

notes: Provider language localizes empty-state and remove-button text.

useWhen: A compact collection of categories or metadata is needed.
Users need to select, remove, or navigate through labeled items.

avoidWhen.situation: A label only communicates status and has no group interaction.
The choices require long labels or explanatory content.
avoidWhen.guidance: Use a less compact selection control.

supportedInteractions: Disable a group or individual items.
Render data-driven collections and empty states.
Standalone action or controlled filter buttons and native navigation links.
Split selected tags with separate deselection and multi-select sub-label menus.
approvedPatterns: Compose Tag Group with Tag children.
Use selection mode when tags act as filters or choices.
Use onRemove with data-driven items for removable collections.
Use href when a tag navigates instead of selecting.
Provide label, description, and error message for field-like groups.
Use TagButton with onPress and optional controlled isSelected outside a collection.
Use TagButton as="a" for standalone navigation with native href, target and rel.
Keep TagDropdown mounted with controlled isSelected and onSelect to animate parent selection; render the single sub-label or count with renderSelection.
limitations: Link tags are neither selectable nor removable.
Complex or render-function content may not yield a useful remove label automatically.
TagDropdown is a standalone split control; do not place it inside TagGroup. Parent-tag membership is consumer owned; deselection clears the sub-label selection first.
Selection callbacks omit link keys; select-all expands to a set of selectable non-link keys when links are present.
accessibility: Give each group a visible label or accessible name.
Provide textValue or removeButtonLabel for icon-only or complex removable tags.
Decorative leading content is hidden from assistive technology.
Error text takes precedence over description text.
Selected disabled tags expose both selected and disabled states; linked tags remain grid rows and describe their destination.
External deselection or disabling closes an open dropdown and restores focus to its label or disabled group; ArrowDown opens the first enabled menu option.
responsive: Tag lists wrap within the available width.
Tag text truncates when a tag reaches its available width.
rtl: Provider language supplies Dhivehi empty and removal text.
